Be forewarned, a project like this is a day's work. It is not hard work, but it is a long process.

A big block of butter.
4 green onions, chopped finely.
1 Spanish onion, diced finely.
1 entire celery stalk, chopped finely.
1 red pepper, chopped coarsely.
2 green peppers, chopped coarsely.
2 carrots, grated finely.
3 jalapeños (or more, whatever floats boats), chopped coarsely.
1 kg (2 lbs-ish) of lean ground beef, browned, drained.
60 ml (1/4 cup-ish) of chili powder of choice.
1 15 ounce can of black beans, washed (the beans, not the fucking can).
1 15 ounce can of kidney beans, washed (still just the beans).
1 15 ounce can of pinto beans, washed (still just the beans).
2 28 ounce cans of diced tomatoes (or even better, 14-ish whole tomatoes, skinned, cleaned out of jelly and seeds, diced, stewed), mashed lightly.
1 bag of tortilla chips, coarsely mashed.
1 can of broth just in case you need liquids.

2 12-inch frying pans.
1 22-quart pot with breathing lid (a hole to let out steam).
1 > foot-long metal spatula, not an icing spatula, not a mixing spatula, a pan-frying spatula.
1 potato masher, gotta fit in your 28 ounce can.

Now, before we move forward, understand the substitutions you can do and still come out well. I clearly say the tomato one, that means you throw away those fucking nasty seeds and that gooey jelly mess. Another easy substitution is for the meat, where you drop a pound or a half a pound for another meat option. Chorizo with the casing removed works great, ground chicken or turkey also work well - beef is just something better, so if you want to do a rocking substitution, go for a fucking honking roast and cube that sucker. You can also add in another can of beans or more tomato for flavour, it is all about what kind of chili you want. Skip the damned baked beans, tomato, maple, or otherwise.

Note, that this produces a large amount of chili, seriously. You will have enough chili for at least 21 servings, so do know that you are going into this with a lot of food coming out. I am serious about the 22-Quart Covered Stockpot. You need to be able to stir your entire chili in that pot with your spatula, if you don't have enough length, you're going to have a bad time.

Pre-dice all that shit - you gotta dice and such, you need this in bowls ready to go.

So, you see here how you need three burners. Big pot on the small burner on the back, the two pans on the big burners. All three burners are on low.

So, grab the tomatoes, if in cans pour the liquids into the pot and then grab yourself a tomato masher. Mash the tomatoes in the cans a little, just to break them up from being giant uniform masses. A couple mashes will do. If freshly diced, you will have a better chili. Then all them tomatoes go in the pot to reduce, lid that shit. The lid is the most important part here, or you will have tomato stains everywhere.

All the veggies get pan fried in butter on one pan or the other as it suits them, pan fry one type of veggie per pan cause they cook at different speeds. Double fist those beautiful vegetables and pour them into your tomatoes as they are caramelized. No seeds from your tomatoes or peppers should go anywhere near your chili, that shit is nasty.

So you're simmering your vegetables then you brown your meats and as they brown, in they go to the veggie-mass. Now that you have added meat to your mix, you add the chili powder.

Water levels will vary at this point, clearly. You want it to be watery to a degree, cause this stuff needs to slow-cook together - so get a can of your broth of choice if you need some more liquid to the mix. And hey, the more broth you add, the longer it must cook, the longer it cooks, the better it tastes.

So, this simmers for at least an hour, stirring every 15 minutes at least (more is better, but don't cream the stuff). You have now got to add the drained and rinsed beans, you can keep the liquids if you are really lazy, but it is not something I go for. And of course, if you did leave in the liquids, you would need to cook longer still.

So, you have your chili, it is now simmering away, becoming chili-er. Stir regularly, every 15 minutes minimum.

Finally, after like 2 more hours have run on, you add your crushed up tortilla chips. And here you have something to take up all that lovely juice. The tortilla chip bits take about 30 minutes to become just another part of the chili, they add to the smell and taste.

After that you can slow cook longer if you want, but you are mostly fine and can serve.

Are waivers granted for any of the medical requirements?

No, NASA does not grant waivers for the medical requirements. When qualifying astronauts for space flight, NASA must look at not only what is required for normal spaceflight operations, but also what each astronaut would require should serious, even life threatening, problems develop. For maximum crew safety, each crewmember must be free of medical conditions that would either impair the person's ability to participate in, or be aggravated by, space flight, as determined by NASA physicians.

Is surgery to improve visual acuity allowed?

As of September 2007, the refractive surgical procedures of the eye, PRK and LASIK, are now allowed, providing at least 1 year has passed since the date of the procedure with no permanent adverse after effects. For those applicants under final consideration, an operative report on the surgical procedure will be requested.

Is flying experience necessary?

Flying experience is not a requirement. The Astronaut Candidate Program requires either 3 years of professional related experience, or 1,000 hours of pilot-in-command time in jet aircraft to meet the minimum qualification requirement. Jet aircraft experience is usually obtained through the military. Any type of flying experience-military or private, is beneficial to have.
